episodes.191951: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a typical summertime environment. A few trees were blown down.
episodes.191979: Two rounds of storms moved through southern New England causing sporadic wind damage mainly in northwestern and north central Massachusetts.
episodes.191980: Two rounds of storms moved through southern New England causing sporadic wind damage mainly in northwestern and north central Massachusetts but also in Connecticut to a lesser extent.
episodes.192013: A hot and humid air mass combined with an approaching cold front helped to spark an isolated thunderstorm that became severe across Greenbrier County. Thunderstorm winds blew down a notable number of trees and also blew a roof off a garage and pushed it away by 500 feet. Hail up to the size of quarters also fell from this storm.
episodes.192014: A hot and humid air mass combined with an approaching cold front helped to produce scattered severe thunderstorms across southwest Virginia. Thunderstorm winds blew down a considerable number of trees and power lines. The winds also knocked down a carport in Buckingham County.
episodes.192017: A severe thunderstorm in northeast Cochise County resulted in a wind gust of 66 mph along Interstate 10 between San Simon and Bowie.
episodes.192033: A favorable placement of the monsoon high over NM and then shifting to the west allowed for an influx of moisture and instability over the state of NM. Daily rounds of of showers and storms starting over the higher terrain midday spreading to lower elevation in the evening before slowly dissipating overnight each day. There were several reports of flash flooding over portions of central NM and a few severe thunderstorm wind gusts.
episodes.192075: An approaching MCV, coupled with ample instability and moisture during the late afternoon and evening hours of July 16, 2024 allowed for convection to begin forming across the Lower Susquehanna Valley.  These thunderstorms quickly began producing instances of severe wind damage across the Lower Susquehanna Valley with isolated instances of small-to-marginally severe hail as they continued tracking northeastward into the Lehigh Valley.
episodes.192076: A cold front stationed across northwestern Pennsylvania with an approaching MCV from the northern panhandle of West Virginia allowed for convection to begin forming across portions of south-central Pennsylvania during the afternoon hours of July 17, 2024. As showers and thunderstorms moved into an environment of more favorable instability and moisture in eastern Pennsylvania, isolated instances of severe thunderstorm winds gusts were observed throughout the late afternoon and evening hours.
episodes.192127: A cold front swept through southern New England causing widespread damage, especially in western and central Massachusetts.
episodes.192159: West-southwesterly flow over Central Alabama with ample moisture return and DCAPE values exceeding 800 J/kg resulted in scattered showers and thunderstorms. A few of the storms were intense enough to produce isolated areas of damage, notably in Talladega County on July 17 and Elmore and Tuscaloosa counties on July 18.
episodes.192204: The synoptic pattern largely remained ridge-dominant continuing on through mid July, but sufficient moisture helped trigger isolated diurnal convection which produced a small number of strong wind gusts across Utah.
episodes.192211: Scattered thunderstorms impacted Middle Tennessee on July 17, 2024. The main hazard with these thunderstorms were strong winds with several trees blown down across the area.
episodes.192218: Showers and thunderstorms led to an isolated instance of flash flooding in Baltimore, Maryland.
episodes.192430: A few widely spaced severe thunderstorms spawned by a stalled front produced localized wind damage across parts of northern and central Virginia and central to northeastern Maryland.
episodes.192431: A few widely spaced severe thunderstorms spawned by a stalled front produced localized wind damage across parts of northern and central Virginia and central to northeastern Maryland.
episodes.192432: A cold front interacting with a hot and humid airmass produced a few loosely organized clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms. Localized wind damage was the main result in the wake of the storms.
episodes.192433: A cold front interacting with a hot and humid airmass produced a few loosely organized clusters of strong to severe thunderstorms. Localized wind damage was the main result in the wake of the storms.
episodes.192440: A stalled front produced clusters of thunderstorms which produced gale to storm force wind gusts over parts of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.192441: A cold front triggered bands of thunderstorms which produced gale force wind gusts over portions of the tidal Potomac River and Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.192454: A disturbance brought a couple of strong to severe thunderstorms across portions of Northeastern Pennsylvania. There were multiple reports of trees down in the Wyoming Valley and Poconos as damaging winds were the main hazard with these storms.
episodes.192468: A slow moving cold front, located near the Arkansas and Missouri borders, set the stage for a dangerous flood event to unfold on the night of the 16th into the morning of the 17th across north-central into central portions of Arkansas. Rainfall amounts of 4 to 9 inches were measured. This much rain in a relatively short amount of time lead to flash flooding, some of which was significant.
episodes.192766: An upper level trough, coupled with strong moisture, produced wet downbursts that brought down a few trees across East Tennessee.
episodes.192784: Showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of a cold front moving through the Ohio Valley.
episodes.192861: An upper trough centered over Canada extended southward over the Midwest and northern and central Plains. Temperatures were in the 80s across south central Nebraska. The atmosphere became uncapped. MLCAPE values were up to 3000 J/kg and effective wind shear was 40 knots. Mid-level lapse rates were fairly modest with values between 6 and 7 degrees C/km. Tornado development was limited by unfavorable low-level wind shear. A cold front was across northern Nebraska. ||Storms developed across south central Nebraska during the afternoon hours and became severe. The storms produced strong, damaging wind gusts in Harlan and Franklin Counties between 3:30 and 4:30 PM CDT then moved southward into northern Kansas. Additional storms developed to the northwest of the area along the cold front and moved into south central Nebraska during the evening hours. One storm moved into Dawson County and began by producing an estimated 60 mph wind gust at 7:45 PM CDT. This storm continued moving south southeast and produced more strong, damaging winds in Dawson, Buffalo, and Phelps Counties. The strongest wind gust was estimated to be near 75 mph in Phelps County. This storm also produced quarter to golf ball sized hail in Dawson and Phelps Counties. There was also a home in Buffalo County that got struck by lightning and was destroyed. The storm reports ended just before 9 PM CDT.
episodes.192974: Southeast Ohio underwent a heatwave during the middle of July with daily chances of showers and strong thunderstorms each afternoon from the 14th through the 17th. Storms extended down from the Great Lakes region by the peak of the afternoon and brought forth strong enough wind gusts to produce downed trees and power lines. Activity then quickly crossed the Ohio River into West Virginia each evening, bringing the severe weather threat to an end.
episodes.193164: Prevailing SW flow over a very moist and unstable airmass produced locally heavy rainfall given weak steering flow and isolated strong thunderstorms with wet downbursts.
episodes.193165: Prevailing SW flow over a very moist and unstable airmass produced locally heavy rainfall given weak steering flow and isolated strong thunderstorms with wet downbursts.
episodes.193167: Prevailing SW flow over a very moist and unstable airmass produced locally heavy rainfall given weak steering flow and isolated strong thunderstorms with wet downbursts.
episodes.193178: Numerous strong to severe thunderstorms developed under northwest flow east of the ridge centered over the Intermountain-West. Storms produced strong winds and half dollar size hail early in the afternoon on the 17th.
episodes.193179: Initial storms early in the afternoon on the 17th produced up to ping pong ball sized as observed in Sioux County Nebraska. Scattered storms eventually organized into a convective line that produced strong outflow winds around 60 mph across the southern Nebraska panhandle late in the afternoon.
episodes.193330: Unusually deep trough across the Great Lakes helped create weak shortwaves across the southeastern US during mid-July. With hot surface temperatures in the mid and upper 90s, an unstable atmosphere developed and resulted in scattered strong to severe thunderstorms on the afternoon and evening of July 17. Microbursts were the primary cause of damaging winds.
episodes.193331: Unusually deep trough across the Great Lakes helped create weak shortwaves across the southeastern US during mid-July. With hot surface temperatures in the mid and upper 90s, an unstable atmosphere developed and resulted in scattered strong to severe thunderstorms on the afternoon and evening of July 17. Microbursts were the primary cause of damaging winds.
episodes.193474: A supercell thunderstorm developed over the southern Black Hills and tracked south-southeast into Fall River County before dissipating over the plains.
episodes.193746: A broken line of thunderstorms developed from northwestern Garden into northeastern Cherry county during the mid afternoon hours of July 16th. As this activity tracked to the southeast, portions of the line became severe, generally south of a line from Logan county, northeast to Brown County. Large hail up to 2 inches in diameter, along with wind gusts to 60 MPH were reported with the strongest storms.
episodes.193761: Scattered to numerous thunderstorms developed along a weak surface boundary across the western half of Oklahoma during the evening of the 16th. Despite strong instability, weak wind shear led to generally disorganized (single/multi-cell) storm modes. A few thunderstorms produced damaging downburst wind events.
episodes.193933: On the evening of the 16th a mesoscale convective system (MCS) developed over the higher terrain of SE CO and NE NM and moved southeast across the OK Panhandle and far northern TX Panhandle. This system put down widespread wind gusts between 58 and 75 mph.  Several of the measured wind gusts were in the 58 to 64 mph range with the 75 being estimated from damaged caused to trees.
episodes.193934: On the evening of the 16th a mesoscale convective system (MCS) developed over the higher terrain of SE CO and NE NM and moved southeast across the OK Panhandle and far northern TX Panhandle. This system put down widespread wind gusts between 58 and 75 mph.  Several of the measured wind gusts were in the 58 to 64 mph range with the 75 being estimated from damaged caused to trees.
episodes.194001: The third and final day of a stretch of hot and humid conditions occurred on July 17, 2024 which reached dangerous levels in Dutchess County with heat index values (feels-like temperatures) reaching 95 to 104 degrees. ||A cold front tracking through eastern New York brought scattered showers and thunderstorms during the afternoon hours resulting in several instances of tree and wire damage, especially in Albany, Saratoga and Columbia counties.
episodes.194007: Early morning thunderstorms produced multiple reports of waterspouts offshore of Panama City on July 17th.
episodes.194027: Thunderstorms developed across east Colorado during the afternoon hours producing penny size hail in Cheyenne county and pea to nickel size hail in Yuma county.
episodes.194028: Thunderstorms developed across western Kansas during the afternoon hours which led to dime to nickel size hail in Sharon Springs along with a 63 mph wind gust in Sherman county.
episodes.194029: Thunderstorms developed across portions of northwest Kansas resulting in 60-65 mph winds and penny size hail mainly across Norton county. The same storms also led to some wind damage in southern Logan county.
episodes.194327: An upper level disturbance dropping south through the Plains along with a weak cold front kicked off a round of showers and thunderstorms across North Texas the afternoon of July 17. A few storms produced microbursts and minor wind damage.
episodes.194389: Extreme rainfall totals occurred during the morning of the 16th in and around Nashville, Illinois, just northwest of the Quad State region, which resulted in a secondary dam failure. Neighboring portions of Jefferson and Perry Counties received 3-6 and 2-5 inches, respectively. Extensive street flooding occurred in Mount Vernon, while some roads north of Tamaroa flooded for the second time within a week. Through the day, flash flooding transitioned to standing water and rising creek levels. Rayse Creek, Beaucoup Creek, and the Little Muddy River rapidly rose and flooded, with a water rescue at a Beaucoup Creek tributary. Rayse Creek at Waltonville reached 17.46 ft, just over 3.5 ft above the previous record. Significant creek flooding continued into the following day. PW values were 2.25 inches in the hardest hit areas with significant moisture transport at 850 mb. A slow-moving west-east boundary was located just to the north, channeling heavy rainfall eastward on the south side.
episodes.194391: Torrential training rainfall redeveloped overnight heading into the 17th, this time over portions of Western Kentucky in the Pennyrile region. Rainfall totals reached 2-7 inches with flooding observed in Livermore, Providence, Madisonville, and several towns in Muhlenberg County. As was the case in the morning, the greater PW values near 2.2 inches had shifted to Western Kentucky, with 850mb moisture transport focused on the area. A slow moving boundary resided to the north, channeling moisture along the boundary on the south side.
episodes.194392: Sub-severe storms formed and moved eastward across the Quad State throughout the day on the 17th. Multiple reports were made of a cold air funnel that formed near Perryville, Missouri.
episodes.194475: Isolated thunderstorms lingered into the evening hours within a typical summertime environment. One storm became strong enough to produce damaging wind gusts and frequent lightning in Effingham County.
episodes.194476: Isolated thunderstorms developed across portions of southeast Georgia in the afternoon hours within a typical summertime environment. The strongest thunderstorm impacted Effingham County with damaging wind gusts and large hail.
episodes.194515: The typical afternoon thunderstorm activity developed across the higher terrain areas of northern and eastern AZ. Most the activity remain anchored over the high terrain with barely any activity observed across the lower elevations given the strong convective inhibition in place. However, with MLCAPE values of around 1000 J/KG, the environment was still favorable for any thunderstorm that developed to become strong. A strong, nearly stationary thunderstorm developed during the evening hours over the Wildcat Burn Scar in northern Maricopa County, dumping rainfall amounts in excess of 1.5 in less than a hour. This was enough rainfall in a short time period to result in flood issues in the burn scar area.
episodes.194534: Around 7 pm, discreet thunderstorms were moving south of Interstate 70 into the smoky hill region, while a more widespread severe line of storms was moving out of Colorado into the far southwest counties. Severe Thunderstorm Watches (#550 and 551) were in effect for the area as the line developed a large bow echo moving east across of most of the area south of highway 400. Numerous severe wind gusts were reported or recorded by spotters and mesonets, including two half dollar size hail reports in the Ford and Spearville areas of Ford county from a supercell that formed ahead of the convective line.
episodes.194634: An isolated strong wind gust was produced by strong to severe thunderstorms in Callahan County.
episodes.194654: A weak trough moving across central GA was able to produce a line of thunderstorms across central GA. Two storms within the line were able to become strong with several trees down.
episodes.194683: An upper low meandered over the region allowind scattered afternoon thunderstorm to develop. A couple became severe.
episodes.194684: An upper low slowly moved across Southeast Texas causing scattered storms. One storm became severe.
episodes.194750: Scattered severe thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced damaging winds across portions of central and south central Virginia.
episodes.194752: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the Chesapeake Bay.
episodes.194753: Scattered thunderstorms well in advance of a cold front produced gusty winds across portions of the James River.
episodes.194875: Scattered thunderstorms developed within northwesterly flow, causing strong outflow winds and wind damage.
episodes.194890: Scattered thunderstorms moved into upstate South Carolina during the evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Spartanburg County.
episodes.194892: Scattered thunderstorms developed across western North Carolina during the afternoon. A few of the storms produced brief severe weather in the form of damaging wind gusts.
episodes.194894: Scattered thunderstorms and storm clusters developed over upstate South Carolina during the evening. One of the storms produced brief damaging wind gusts in Greenville County.
episodes.194914: Scattered thunderstorms developed and quickly intensified in the afternoon on July 17th across Northeast Texas into Southwest Arkansas, in the vicinity of a surface boundary and to the south of a mesoscale convective vortex (MCV) shifting slowly southeastward across Central Oklahoma. Strong heating of a richly moist airmass resulted in MLCAPE increasing to 1500-3000 J/kg. Low/mid-level flow was weak across the region, but large precipitable water values and steepening low-level lapse rates were supportive of some potential for localized downbursts. A lone severe thunderstorm produced very localized wind damage in Columbia County Arkansas.
episodes.194950: Scattered storms developed across the region each day. Some gusty winds occurred from this activity and a few locations saw some downed trees.
episodes.194965: Monsoon moisture fueled isolated thunderstorms over northwest Arizona. One produced high winds.
episodes.194993: A mesoscale convective vortex pushed into the Missouri Ozarks during the afternoon of July 16, 2024, resulting in showers and thunderstorms developing out ahead of it. Thunderstorm coverage and intensity increased during the overnight hours and into the early morning hours of July 17 as they developed along a stationary boundary situated west to east on the Missouri/Arkansas border. Thunderstorms first formed over northeast Oklahoma and continued to spread east into far southern Missouri, resulting in training thunderstorms producing heavy rainfall and flash flooding. Rainfall amounts between 4.0 and 8.61 inches were measured across portions of the Missouri Ozarks, with Taney County experiencing the higher end of that range. Turkey Creek in Hollister crested at 14.65 feet, causing evacuations along the creek, flooded cars and RVs, and a washed out bridge. Additionally, the first floor of City Hall in Branson was flooded, with multiple roadways flooded and damaged between Branson and Hollister in Taney County.
episodes.195012: Unseasonably cool weather overtook the Great Lakes region behind an unseasonably strong cold front July 16-17. Scattered lake effect rain showers and non-severe thunderstorms were a result of this. Fall-like setup over the warm waters of the Great Lakes also favored development of waterspouts.
episodes.195020: A large MCS formed across New York state on the afternoon of July 16th.  This complex continued to move eastward and held its structure as it reached New Hampshire by early evening.  Bowing line segments caused multiple microbursts and high end wind damage.  At the north end of the squall line, a bookend vortex developed just north of Hanover, where a tornado briefly touched down, causing damage.
episodes.195031: A broad positively tilted upper-level trough approached from the west along with associated surface cold front and pre-frontal trough. The pre-frontal trough moved into an area with high instability (1750-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE). This combined with Effect Bulk Shear values around 25 kt allowed for multiple severe thunderstorms to develop. The storms were able to produce damaging wind gusts across southeast NY, with DCAPE values around 750-1000 J/kg.
episodes.195032: A broad positively tilted upper-level trough approached from the west along with associated surface cold front and pre-frontal trough. The pre-frontal trough moved into an area with high instability (1750-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE). This combined with Effect Bulk Shear values around 25 kt allowed for multiple severe thunderstorms to develop. The storms were able to produce damaging wind gusts across southern CT, with DCAPE values around 750-1000 J/kg.
episodes.195035: A broad positively tilted upper-level trough approached from the west along with associated surface cold front and pre-frontal trough. The pre-frontal trough moved into an area with high instability (1750-2000 J/kg of MLCAPE). This combined with Effect Bulk Shear values around 25 kt allowed for multiple severe thunderstorms to develop. The storms were able to produce damaging wind gusts across the waters, with DCAPE values around 750-1000 J/kg.
episodes.195052: A large MCS formed across New York state on the afternoon of July 16th. This complex continued to move eastward and held its structure as it reached New Hampshire by early evening. The complex began to weaken by late evening when it reached York and Cumberland County Maine.  Isolated wind damage was reported as the storms began to weaken across the area.
episodes.195058: A weak frontal boundary pushed though Central Maine during the afternoon hours of July 17th, sparking numerous showers and thunderstorms.  A weak shear environment prevented most storms from becoming severe, but an isolated storm brought some damaging winds to Androscoggin County.
episodes.195064: A cluster of thunderstorms formed during the afternoon across southeast Louisiana in response to high moisture and instability. This cluster of storms were able to take advantage of mid-level dry air to produce severe winds across the Florida parishes and marine areas before pushing into the southshore and producing flash flooding.
episodes.195065: A cluster of thunderstorms formed during the afternoon across southeast Louisiana in response to high moisture and instability. This cluster of storms were able to take advantage of mid-level dry air to produce severe winds across the Florida parishes and marine areas before pushing into the southshore and producing flash flooding.
episodes.195074: A weak frontal boundary pushed though Central New Hampshire during the afternoon hours of July 17th, sparking numerous showers and thunderstorms. A weak shear environment prevented most storms from becoming severe, but a few isolated pulse severe thunderstorms were able to develop.
episodes.195091: Deep monsoon moisture over northern Arizona with light steering winds brought locally heavy rain to parts of the area.
episodes.195193: A strong shortwave and surface trough approached eastern Pennsylvania. The incoming disturbance encountered a very warm, moist, and unstable airmass. The result was several strong to severe thunderstorms developing, producing damaging wind gusts and downing several trees and power lines in eastern Pennsylvania. Large hail was also reported.
episodes.195194: A strong shortwave and surface trough approached the Mid-Atlantic. The incoming disturbance encountered a very warm, moist, and unstable airmass. The result was several strong to severe thunderstorms developing, producing damaging wind gusts and downing several trees and power lines in New Jersey.
episodes.195196: A strong shortwave and surface trough approached the Mid-Atlantic. The incoming disturbance encountered a very warm, moist, and unstable airmass. The result was  strong to severe thunderstorms developing, producing damaging wind gusts and downing trees and power lines in eastern Maryland.
episodes.195197: A strong shortwave and surface trough approached the Mid-Atlantic. The incoming disturbance encountered a very warm, moist, and unstable airmass. The result was strong to severe thunderstorms developing, producing damaging wind gusts and downing trees and power lines in Delaware.
episodes.195198: A cold front approached with a hot and humid airmass in place. The result was several strong to severe thunderstorms developing, producing damaging wind gusts across portions of eastern Pennsylvania. Some large hail was reported as well.
episodes.195199: A cold front approached with a hot and humid airmass in place. The result was several strong to severe thunderstorms developing, producing damaging wind gusts across portions of New Jersey.
episodes.195217: A cluster of showers and thunderstorms developed along the Ohio River just after sunset on July 16th. This cluster of storms grew upscale quickly, extending back into western Kentucky before gradually pushing off to the south and east through the nighttime hours. While most of the convection did not produce severe weather, a strong storm which developed over Bullitt County produced scattered wind damage across Bullitt and Nelson County.
episodes.195244: A shortwave trough traversing the Pacific Northwest brought increasing instability and moisture across the region, resulting in thunderstorms developing across portions of central and north central Oregon the afternoon of July 16th.
episodes.195245: A shortwave trough continued across central Oregon into central and eastern Washington, resulting in convective activity from the previous day moving north into this area. While most storms produced weak gusty outflows, a storm in the Goldendale area produced strong winds that resulted in property damage.
episodes.195256: Scattered to numerous showers and strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon hours ahead of a pre-frontal trough axis moving into central Tennessee and NW Alabama. Some of these produced widespread damaging wind damage in portions of Limestone and Jackson counties.
